body:
`person:group-dhfl-wadhawan` · flag: **severe** · confidence: verified · tickers: DHFL

Flag: SEVERE. Dewan Housing Finance (DHFL), once India's third-largest housing financier, collapsed in 2019 after the IL&FS-triggered funding freeze and a Cobrapost exposé (Jan-2019) alleging ~Rs 31,000 cr routed to shell companies. RBI superseded the board (Nov-2019); first NBFC resolved under IBC -- Piramal acquired it (Sep-2021); public equity was extinguished. Findings: SEBI's final order (12-Aug-2025, 181 pages) held that from 2006 to Mar-2019 DHFL promoters/executives diverted ~Rs 14,040 cr to 'Bandra Book Entities' (Wadhawan-linked firms) disguised as retail housing loans in a hidden branch-level book; it barred Kapil and Dheeraj Wadhawan for 5 years (Rs 27 cr fine each) and Rakesh and Sarang Wadhawan for 4 years (Rs 20.75 cr each), ~Rs 120 cr fines in all. CBI's ~Rs 34,926 cr bank-consortium fraud case (2022; UBI-led 17 banks) is in trial; the Supreme Court granted the brothers bail (Dec-2025) citing trial delay; a Delhi court refused CBI's plea to add charges (Oct-2026, single-source). The Yes Bank link: Yes Bank invested ~Rs 3,700 cr in DHFL debt in 2018 allegedly in return for ~Rs 600 cr loan to a Rana Kapoor family firm (CBI allegation). Wadhawans were earlier tied to HDIL/PMC Bank fraud. Early signals: loan growth far above peers with thin disclosure, large 'project loans' to opaque builders, wholesale funding mismatch, and an auditor/whistleblower trail.

- **regulator findings:** SEBI Aug-2025: Rs 14,040 cr diverted; bans and Rs ~120 cr fines

Sources:

`insight:nse-factor-indices-quality-lowvol-momentum` | confidence: verified | date: 2026-10-30

Primary NSE Indices data (TR = total return; base 1 Apr 2005). Nifty200 Momentum 30 (whitepaper data to 27 Feb 2026): 19.19% CAGR since inception vs 15.08% for Nifty 200, at higher volatility; maximum drawdowns of momentum indices 68% (Nifty200 Mom 30), 73% (Midcap150 Mom 50), 70% (Nifty500 Mom 50) vs 64%, 73%, 64% for parents - 'momentum strategies ... thrive in trending markets but face challenges during market reversals.' Factsheets as of 30 Oct 2026: Nifty200 Momentum 30 TR 18.05% since 2005 but 7.93% over 5 years and -8.48% over 1 year (vol 22.3% since inception); Nifty200 Quality 30 TR 16.58% since 2005 (5y 6.96%, 1y -8.86%; vol 17.9%, beta 0.79 vs Nifty 50); Nifty500 Value 50 TR 10.28% since 2005, 5y -1.93%, 1y -19.56% (vol 27.2%); Nifty 50 TR 12.15% since Nov-1995 (5y 6.70%, 1y -9.45%, YTD-2026 -10.91%; P/E 19.3). Nifty500 Multifactor MQVLv 50 (momentum+quality+value+low-vol, data to 31 Dec 2024): 21.11% CAGR since 2005 vs 14.97% for Nifty 500 TR, at lower volatility (17.4% vs 20.6%); positive in 100% of rolling 5-year windows but negative in 15.5% of 1-year windows (worst -48.6%). Lessons: quality/low-vol give most of the premium with smaller drawdowns; momentum and value are cyclical (2026 drawdown hit both); all are back-tested from 2005 for indices launched 2018-2024 (look-ahead/selection bias in launch timing). Actionable: a quality/low-vol core is a reasonable passive baseline to beat before claiming stock-picking skill.

Sources:

**Ten-year shape `[SCR]` consolidated:**
| FY | Sales | OPM | Other inc. | PAT | EPS | CFO | FCF |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| FY17 | 1,456 | 10.0% | 8 | 65 | 3.62 | −18 | −48 |
| FY18 | 2,018 | 11.7% | 17 | 129 | 7.14 | 117 | 21 |
| FY19 | 2,186 | 10.8% | 11 | 110 | 6.12 | 177 | 46 |
| FY20 | 1,758 | 9.7% | 11 | 92 | 5.11 | 209 | 67 |
| FY21 | 1,892 | 13.4% | 11 | 141 | 7.80 | 223 | 170 |
| FY22 | 2,698 | 14.8% | 5 | 217 | 12.04 | 43 | −296 |
| FY23 | 3,488 | 12.8% | **1,201** | 1,115 | 61.89 | 278 | 109 |
| FY24 | 3,415 | 11.0% | 8 | 144 | 7.96 | 244 | 119 |
| FY25 | 3,536 | 11.0% | 17 | 162 | 8.99 | 192 | 104 |
| FY26 | 3,939 | 12.1% | 9 | 202 | 11.23 | 390 | 262 |
| TTM Sep-26 | 4,144 | 11.9% | 15 | 219 | 12.15 | — | — |

**Adjustments that matter:**
- **FY23 is a one-off.** ₹1,201 cr other income = the LMEL award gain. Core PAT ≈ ₹215 cr [EST: PBT 1,485 − 1,201 + ~5 normal OI, × 0.75], so core EPS is ~12.0.
- **FY26 PAT is understated by ~₹34 cr.** Exceptional item −₹8.7 cr, and ₹25.1 cr of deferred tax from earlier years (Q4 tax rate 58%) `[AR26 P&L]`. Normalised FY26 PAT ≈ ₹230 cr.
- **ROCE/ROE on screener (4%/2%) are meaningless.** The denominator holds the LMEL mark: investments ₹11,369 cr standalone / ₹11,359 cr consolidated at Sep-2026 `[Q2FY27]`, plus
  a **deferred tax liability of ₹1,639 cr**, which is mostly on the MTM. **Operating ROCE** ≈ EBIT 364 ÷ (FA 1,577 + CWIP 214 + NWC ~750 [EST]) ≈ **14% pre-tax,
  ~10.7% post-tax**. That is about the cost of equity.
- **Book value ₹672/share (P/B 0.55)** is ~85% LMEL mark net of DTL. It is not a measure of steel-business value.
- **Customer concentration:** no customer ≥10% in FY25 or FY26. Exports ₹114 cr (2.9%) vs ₹48 cr `[AR26 n.25a]`.
- **Other-income decomposition FY26 `[AR26 n.25b]`:** interest 9.85, LMEL dividend 6.00, insurance/other 0.5 → core PBT (ex OI) ≈ ₹283 cr.
- **H1 FY27 `[Q2FY27]`:** standalone revenue ₹2,201 cr (+10.3%), PBT ₹164 cr (+17%), PAT ₹112 cr. **CFO ₹339 cr is flattered by trade payables
  +₹191 cr** (good but misleading). Long-term debt repaid ₹79 cr; net debt fell from ~₹245 cr (Mar-26: borrowings ₹475 cr − cash/bank ₹230 cr) to **₹26 cr** (Sep-26).
- **Quarterly OPM `[SCR]`** (Sep-23 → Sep-26): 12,11,11,9,11,12,11,12,10,14,12,11,11%. H2 runs above H1 by 1.5–2.5 pp in FY25 and FY26.
